nodes.description: Abnormal formation of the embryonic heart. In zebrafish, depletion of flt4 reduces heart size and alters heart looping; wild-type human FLT4 mRNA rescues this, while mRNA carrying tetralogy-associated variants rescues it incompletely or not at all. In patients the result is a conotruncal or outflow-tract defect, most often tetralogy of Fallot.

ClinGen split this disease from Milroy disease partly on mechanism, loss of function here against the dominant negative kinase-dead alleles of Milroy disease.

nodes.description: Homozygous knockout mice die in utero with defective vasculature formation; heterozygous mice are normal.

Missense FLT4 variants found in patients with tetralogy of Fallot, expressed in primary human endothelial cells, cause the receptor to aggregate in the perinuclear endoplasmic reticulum and activate proteostatic and metabolic signaling. Milroy disease variants and wild-type FLT4 do not. The variant cells show altered expression in developmental signaling pathways, and inhibiting proteostatic signaling abrogates these effects. This is a mechanism for the missense subset of alleles, distinct from the dominant negative mechanism of Milroy alleles.
